claims.text: Hierarchical TiO2 containing lubricant-filled pores or channels can balance mechanical strength and lubrication efficiency.
The proposed hierarchical TiO2 can provide stable tribological performance over a wide temperature range.
The initial TiO2 is polycrystalline with an average grain size of 100 nm.
A combination of 3D printing and infiltration can create a hierarchical TiO2 microstructure containing lubricant-filled pores or channels.
The lubricant-filled pores or channels have diameters of 1–10 μm.
Lubricant-filled pores or channels continuously supply lubricant to the contact surface.
Continuous lubricant delivery from the pores or channels reduces friction.
Continuous lubricant delivery from the pores or channels reduces wear.
The hierarchical TiO2 microstructure maintains mechanical strength and stability.
Under 25–500°C, 1 MPa, and 1 m/s sliding, the hierarchical material will reduce friction coefficient by 30% relative to conventional uniform-microstructure TiO2.
Under 25–500°C, 1 MPa, and 1 m/s sliding, the hierarchical material will reduce wear rate by 50% relative to conventional uniform-microstructure TiO2.
The reductions in friction coefficient and wear rate depend on the specific lubricant and processing conditions.
